question.text: \(\mathrm{n}\) objects are distributed at random among \(\mathrm{n}\) persons. The number of ways in which this can be done so that at least one of them will not get any object is

solution.text:
Hint : Total number of ways of distributing \(n\) objects randomly among \(n\) persons \(=\mathrm{n}^n\)
Number of ways in which each person gets exactly one object \(={ }^n P_n=n\) !
\(\therefore\) Required number of ways \(=n^n-n\) !
